scenario: AITA for deleting my stepbrothers profile on my Nintendo switch? | At the beginning of the school year I had to watch my stepbrother for a week while my dad and his mom went on a trip to help out her parents with something. Brought my switch with me because my school is more than an hour away and I wanted something to do on the train during my commute everyday. My stepbrother wanted to play on it. Him being so into it actually turned into a big help to distract him while I studied, so I made a new profile on it for him so he wouldn’t mess up my saves. When I got back to school I eventually got annoyed with having to click on my profile each time I started a game and each time I went to the eshop. So I just deleted his profile. So, this early this morning I got on the train to go to my dads for thanksgiving. I usually go home to my moms, but she and my stepdad are going to see his family and Im not up for going plane trip. Anyway I brought my switch again for the train ride. Just a little while ago my stepbrother picked it up to start playing and came into the kitchen, where I was talking with my dad, freaking out because his Zelda save was gone and he wanted me to help him fix it. When I told him I deleted it he started crying. Like not full on crying, but his eyes were watery a little and red. Now he’s holed up in his room. My dad thinks it was mean of me to delete it because I know my stepbrother was enjoying playing it. I didn’t think it was a big deal since I usually never bring my switch over when I visit.

message.reasoning:
Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether the action in this scenario is morally acceptable or not. Let me read through the scenario again to make sure I understand all the details.

So, the person in question is a student who had to watch their stepbrother for a week while their dad and stepbrother's mom went on a trip. They brought their Nintendo Switch because they have a long commute to school, and it helps pass the time. The stepbrother wanted to play on the Switch, and it turned out to be helpful because it distracted him while the person studied. So, they created a new profile for the stepbrother to prevent him from messing up their saves.

After the week was over, the person went back to school and found themselves annoyed every time they had to switch profiles to play their games or access the eShop. So, they decided to delete the stepbrother's profile. Now, during Thanksgiving, the stepbrother found out his Zelda save was gone and got upset, even crying a little. The dad thinks it was mean to delete the profile, knowing the stepbrother was enjoying playing.

Alright, so the main action in question is deleting the stepbrother's profile on the Nintendo Switch. The person did this because they were annoyed by having to switch profiles every time they used the Switch. The stepbrother was upset because he lost his save, and the dad thinks it was mean.

I need to evaluate whether this action is morally acceptable or not. Let's break it down.

First, the person created the profile to help the stepbrother and to keep their own games safe. That seems considerate. But then, after the week, they found it annoying to switch profiles, so they deleted it. The stepbrother was using the profile, and deleting it caused him to lose his save, which made him upset.

So, the action of deleting the profile without informing the stepbrother seems to have caused harm. The person knew the stepbrother was enjoying playing, but they still went ahead and deleted the profile. That might be seen as selfish or inconsiderate.

On the other hand, the person might have felt that the profile was only temporary and that they had the right to manage their own Switch. They might have thought it wasn't a big deal since they usually don't bring the Switch over when visiting. But the stepbrother was using it, and the deletion affected him emotionally.

I think the key points here are consent and consideration. The person created the profile for the stepbrother, but then deleted it without discussing it with him. The stepbrother had a legitimate use for the profile, and deleting it without warning caused him distress.

So, from a moral standpoint, deleting the profile without informing the stepbrother and considering his feelings seems unacceptable. It shows a lack of empathy and consideration for the stepbrother's feelings and interests.

Therefore, the action is morally unacceptable.
